result.question: For a Python Lifecycle Hook container, which component type and ArtifactService Publish Type should I choose, and which CI step must be enabled?
result.answer:
- For a Python Lifecycle Hook, select the component type MICROSERVICE_PYTHON_COMMON_COMPONENT in your PipelineHub project. [doc-0108]
- Set the ArtifactService Publish Type to None for Lifecycle Hooks. [doc-0108]
- Configure the CI steps to include the Publish step, which builds the Lifecycle Hooks as Docker containers. [doc-0108]

retrieved_sources.title: Lifecycle hooks CI/CD
retrieved_sources.text:
**Overview:**
-------------

This document outlines how to configure CI/CD for Lifecycle Hooks and subsequently consume them using PIPELINEHUB.

**Usecase:**
------------

This guide focuses on building a Lifecycle Hook as a Docker container and publishing it to the CloudNative Platform, enabling other microservices to utilize it afterward.

**Source code languages supported:**
------------------------------------

PipelineHub supports signal handlers written in Java, Python, Go, and Golang

**Configuration Steps:**
------------------------

### Step 1: Configure the right component type in your PipelineHub project

Involves choosing the right component type in your PipelineHub Project, one of depending on the source code language:

* **MICROSERVICE_JAVA_COMMON_COMPONENT**
* **MICROSERVICE_GO_COMMON_COMPONENT**
* **MICROSERVICE_GOLANG_COMMON_COMPONENT**
* **MICROSERVICE_PYTHON_COMMON_COMPONENT**

### Step 2: Configure ArtifactService publish type

Choose the **ArtifactService Publish Type as "None"** and save.

retrieved_sources.title: Lifecycle hooks CI/CD
retrieved_sources.text:
### Step 3: Include Publish Step in CI and trigger pipeline

Configure the CI steps to include **Publish** step, then trigger the pipeline. This will build the Lifecycle Hooks and produce them as Docker containers.

### Step 4: Reference Lifecycle Hooks in the Spec File of Another Workload Artifact

In the target workload artifact (e.g., a microservice application component) where the generated Lifecycle Hooks should be applied -

#### Step 4.1: Modify the osspArtifact.yaml File to Include Lifecycle Hooks

In the **lifecycleHooks** section of the osspArtifact.yaml file (for the target workload artifact, a microservice application component), refer to the [Build Artifact Reference Resolution User Guide - BOM Format Instructions](#) for detailed guidance on how to substitute the newly generated Docker image.

#### Step 4.2 Trigger pipeline

Initiate the pipeline for this component. The Lifecycle Hooks from **Step 3** will be included in the artifact publish output.

**Reporting Details:**
----------------------

Step 2
------

Involves choosing the right component type in your PipelineHub Project, one of depending on the source code language:

* **MICROSERVICE_JAVA_COMMON_COMPONENT**
* **MICROSERVICE_GO_COMMON_COMPONENT**
* **MICROSERVICE_GOLANG_COMMON_COMPONENT**
* **MICROSERVICE_PYTHON_COMMON_COMPONENT**

Step 3
------

Choose the **ArtifactService Publish Type as "Signal Handler"** and specify the path of your signalHandlerSpec file (relative to source folder path) in the source repo in **"ArtifactService Specification (JSON File Name)**" field  

**Reporting Details:**
----------------------

As part of this initial rollout, PipelineHub only supports CD for signal handlers where a single docker container is produced as part of Common Component CI. Support for multiple docker containers is part of our upcoming sprints.

retrieved_sources.title: ArtifactService Specification Component Type - (CI/CD for Associations/TransactionDatabase Configs/EnvironmentService Proxy)
retrieved_sources.text:
**Component Type / Example Usecases**
-------------------------------------

#### **Type**

A new component type **“ArtifactService Specification (No Code)”** is being introduced under CloudNative Project Type

* Serves usecases with only a ArtifactService specification file in the source repo that needs to published as an ArtifactService Artifact (Workload/Generic/Signal Handler)
* A new parameter "ArtifactService Publish Type", which will dictate the ArtifactService publishing process. Following are the possible ArtifactService Publish Types:

	+ Workload Artifact
	+ Generic Artifact
	+ Signal Handler
	+ None

#### **Usecases**

**Workload Artifacts (Configs/Secrets Only):**

Example:  TransactionDatabase Config & Secrets

| Component Type | ArtifactService Publish Type | Comments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ArtifactService Specification Only (No Code) | Workload Artifact | eg: * **<https://app.example.com/reference/resource-681>**
* **<https://app.example.com/reference/resource-682>**
 |
